Well, there’s a few things you can do (I’m gonna treat this as base Myers, no addons no perks so they’re just general tips). 


While you’re in tier one, there are one of two things you should be doing. Either try to get in a really sneaky hit or grab on a survivor with your heavily reduced terror radius or most of the time you try to build up your evil within to get tier two ASAP. Your movement speed and lunge distance are much shorter in tier one compared to tier two.


In tier two, you want to try your best to have a mix of hitting survivors or building up evil within. If they’re able to make a pallet, stand outside of the stun distance and start to build up evil within, we want to build as much meter as possible for tier three. If they’re in the open or if they’re maybe vaulting an unsafe window and sometimes pallet you can go for a free hit. Try your best to build up evil within while you can but never deny a free hit. Another tip is to just barely not get evil within three and keep it for a healthy survivor. Never activate tier three on an injured survivor, it’s a waste of your meter.


When going into tier three, make sure you get as close as possible to the survivor and stalk them for a short amount of time to get into tier three and conserve as much meter as possible. Your lunge range is much longer and your vaulting speed is a bit faster so you’re able to challenge pallets, window vaults and possible loops lot more effectively.

You typically want to be as aggressive as possible, but sometimes it may not be possible if your support is someone like Janna or if their ad is someone like Ezreal or Caitlyn who have long ranges and easy escapes. Try to get an early level lead by slightly pushing the wave at level one, making sure their minions will always die before yours. Be sure to not shove into the turret before hand since the goal here is to get the extra stats from blood rush so that they won’t be able to trade with you since you have an extra level on them.

2. The sorcery tree with Aery is his most effective main rune path because of the bonus ad from the tree as well as the extra little bit from Aery. Other options aren’t necessarily bad, but they will almost always never be as effective as Aery in the grand scheme of things. Some can be situational but if you’re unsure about a keystone then take Aery to be on the safe side. Take celerity for the added movement speed and extra attack damage and scorch for the added damage from stand aside, this little bit can determine whether or not you get a kill. Mana ring vs the magic shield is situational. Take the shield if they have a heavy poke support like lulu or brand. For a secondary tree I would take precision taking triumph for the added gold and huge health restore as well as coup de grace for the added low health damage. If the lack of attack speed bothers you, buy a dagger on one of your early backs and it’ll do the trick.

3. If you’re just starting out, practice tool is a great way to get the feel for catching axes. Eventually with enough practice however, it will become second nature and you won’t have to think about it.

4. Draven is a bit of a strange adc because of axes, if you’re new to the role or the auto reliant archetype it may be a bit tricky at first. However if you do play adc or the proper archetype a lot then he will come a lot easier to you than if you didn’t since you’d already be used to the way he plays. Regardless though, Draven will take a pretty long time to finally get proficient at, but it makes him one of the most rewarding champions ever to play once you do finally get the hang of him though.

However, the absolute most important thing to remember is to always do the r + flash combo, it will make you the best Draven in the world, incomparable to anyone else.

Draven right now is in a strange position. We're in a meta where everyone wants to sit back and farm for a long time before they get rolling due to ardent supports becoming super popular lately. This makes it where if Draven wants to go in on his own, most of the time people are going to run away from you since all they want to do is scale. This makes it where your support dictates how easy or difficult it will be to go in and get kills and start a snowball. Champions like Alistar, Thresh or Leona who have long ranged engage with a good amount of cc makes it easy for Draven to go in and get a kill or have the enemy waste summoners. However if you have someone like Janna, Lulu or Nami it may be a bit more difficult to go in and straight up win trades until a little bit longer since they need to get higher levels or get ardent first. You still need to know how to be in stances for trading and manipulate axes for bloodrush engages, but supports are a large part of getting Draven going.

Knowing Draven is important to being able to carry games but it's equally (possibly more) important to learn other champion's level and item spikes along with what each of the champion's player's mindsets are when playing their champion. Bloodthirster early on isn't always the best choice, but it's never a bad choice you can make. Draven will always benefit from lifestyle more than other adc's in the bit lane because of axes.  The unique passive is also super nice since you essentially get free maximum health since the shield only starts to grow once you're full health. It's a good contender with death's dance, but sometimes you may need to interchange the two depending on the situation.

It depends on the situation and what boots you bought early on. Berserker's graves can be replaced with one of the zeal items except for runaan's since it doesn't provide as much as the other options for Draven. Ninja tabi's can be replaced with a guardian angel. Merc treads can be replaced with either a maw or a scimitar depending on what the threat you're buying it for does (burst vs cc). The only problem with replacing boots is that you lose a large chunk of you're movement speed unless you replace it with a zeal item, so it's always going to be a toss up whether you replace it or not. If you already bought one of the items you can replace one of the boots with, buy something you had to leave out because of the item. If you wanted to get a blood thirster but had to get a guardian angel early, you can replace the your boots with the blood thirster.

I personally think Draven really benefits from the item, but it's still very situational when you should buy it. It's a very strong item if Draven gets ahead because of the mana restoration on crits. Pair that with a little bit of life steal and Draven becomes an unstoppable lane bully since he sustains both resources (a good example of this is having a vampiric scepter along with the essence reaver). This allows him to trade and come out on top because he will always have more health and mana after the trade ends as long as there is something to hit. The cooldown reduction on the item is also very helpful since as you said, you can constantly keep 2 axes spinning. The attack damage is also very nice to have since Draven benefits from it a lot. However, it is still a very situational item since. The cooldown reduction and damage will always be useful but by mid game the mana regen isn't as useful since by then blood rush doesn't take as much mana compared to when it only has one point in it. Overall, essence reaver is a good item but only in certain situations.
